Pages for relationships, work, and personal fulfillment.
For each area: list your strengths, recall when they helped, and plan two new ways to use them.

title: The Autism-Dissociation Association
description: Slides from an Autscape 2023 talk on how autism and dissociation connect, which recasts trauma as 'Chronic Unaddressed Toxic Stress' (CUTS).
citation: Titman, N. (2023). *The autism-dissociation association* [Conference presentation]. Autscape 2023. https://www.autscape.org/2023/programme/handouts/autscape-2023-autism-dissociation-association.pdf

view.overview: Slides from Nat Titman’s Autscape 2023 talk on how autism and dissociation are connected.
keyPoints: What dissociation is, and the main dissociative experiences and disorders.
Why dissociative disorders may be more common among autistic people.
An alternative to the ACEs lens: chronic unaddressed toxic stress (CUTS).
Autistic experiences such as burnout, inertia, and alexithymia, seen through a dissociation lens.
view.why: These slides belong to their presenter, and the host site keeps the official copy.

keyPoints: A triangle diagram linking a situation to thoughts, emotions, and behaviors.

Useful for introducing CBT.

title: Venn Diagram - ADHD & Anxiety
description: A Venn diagram showing the shared and distinct symptoms of ADHD and Anxiety.
citation: Neurodivergent Insights. (n.d.). *ADHD vs. Anxiety*. Retrieved from https://neurodivergentinsights.com/adhdvsanxiety/

view.overview: A Venn diagram by Dr. Neff comparing ADHD and generalized anxiety.
keyPoints: What leans ADHD (novelty-seeking, attention regulation) and what leans anxiety (persistent, outsized worry).
A large overlap in focus, sleep, fatigue, restlessness, and irritability.
Helps explain why anxiety can be mistaken for ADHD, and the reverse.
view.why: Neurodivergent Insights doesn’t give permission for other websites to repost its graphics and guides.

title: Venn Diagram - ADHD & Autism
description: A Venn diagram illustrating the overlapping and distinct traits of ADHD and Autism.
citation: Neurodivergent Insights. (n.d.). *ADHD vs. Autism*. Retrieved from https://neurodivergentinsights.com/adhd-vs-autism/

view.overview: A Venn diagram by Dr. Megan Anna Neff (Neurodivergent Insights) comparing ADHD and autism, from her Misdiagnosis Monday series.
keyPoints: What tends to be more ADHD (for example, seeking novelty) and more autism (for example, seeking familiarity and routine).
A large shared middle, including sensory differences, emotional regulation, executive function, and masking.
Useful for seeing why the two get confused, or happen together.
view.why: Neurodivergent Insights doesn’t give permission for other websites to repost its graphics and guides.

title: Venn Diagram - ADHD, Autism & Anxiety

view.overview: A three-way Venn diagram comparing ADHD, autism, and anxiety, made by the Tumblr creator @tfw-adhd.
keyPoints: Traits typical of each condition.
Overlaps between ADHD and autism, such as sensory issues and hyperfixations.
A shared center including distractibility, rejection sensitivity, and stimming.

title: Venn Diagram - ADHD, Autism & OCD
description: A Venn diagram comparing the traits of ADHD, Autism, and OCD, highlighting areas of convergence and distinction.

view.overview: A three-way Venn diagram by Dr. Neff comparing ADHD, autism, and OCD.
keyPoints: Traits that lean toward each condition, and where each pair overlaps.
A shared center that includes intrusive thoughts, sensory differences, sleep trouble, and executive function.
A reminder that these often co-occur.
view.why: Neurodivergent Insights doesn’t give permission for other websites to repost its graphics and guides.

title: Venn Diagram - ADHD, Autism & PTSD

view.overview: A three-way Venn diagram with a trait table comparing autism, ADHD, and PTSD, marked “©Keech 2022.”
keyPoints: Traits for each condition, such as flashbacks and hypervigilance for PTSD.
Overlaps between each pair.
A shared center including stimming, interoception differences, and higher risk of victimization.
view.why: This graphic belongs to its creator (Keech), who hasn’t given permission to repost it.

view.overview: A Venn diagram from Dr. Neff’s Misdiagnosis Monday series comparing social anxiety and autism.
keyPoints: What tends to point toward social anxiety, and what tends to point toward autism.
Where the two overlap, which is part of why they’re mixed up.
Useful when sorting out why social situations feel hard.

title: WALKS the TALK: A Skill for Receiving Feedback
description: A worksheet outlining the WALKS the TALK practice to help individuals, especially those who are self-critical, respond to feedback more effectively.
citation: ACT with Compassion. (n.d.). *Helping people who are highly self-critical benefit from feedback*. Retrieved from https://www.actwithcompassion.com/helping_people_who_are_highly_self_critical_benefit_from_feedback

view.overview: An ACT with Compassion skill handout for taking in feedback when you’re prone to shame, built around the acronym WALKS the TALK.
keyPoints: Noticing feedback and your emotional reaction to it.
Listening openly and looking for the kernel of truth.
Pausing and soothing yourself before deciding what to accept.
Acting on it with kindness toward yourself.
